full_judgment: 5. It appears that the learned Judges of the High Court Division independently on consideration of the oral evidence on record found that the defendants were in possession of the suit land to the exclusion of the plaintiffs and their vendors and the suit was barred by limitation as because the plaintiff did not file the suit within 12 years from the date of defendant's possession. The learned Judges of the High Court Division correctly found that the plaintiff's case was not that the defendants are possessing on behalf of the original owner Satish Chandra Chakravarty and his brother or their vendee Protab Chandra. As a matter of fact the defendants are in possession claiming a hostile title against the lawful owners and in that view of the matter the learned Judges found that defendant No. 1 had been in possession since 1936 and had constructed an incomplete two storied building. The learned Judges on consideration of the oral evidence of the defendant's witnesses as well as from the plaintiff's witnesses found that Satish Chandra left the country keeping the suit property uncared for during the communal disturbance of 1950 and never returned. Taking advantage of this defendant No. 1 entered into possession at least at that time and since then he is in continuous and uninterrupted possession of the land and building to the exclusion of Satish Chandra Protab Chandra Bhattacharjee and plaintiff Arshid Ali. Further, the learned Judges considered the admission of P.W.1 Arshid Ali and the statement of D.W. 6 Washimuddin Mia that defendant No. 1 is in possession from before January, 1954. The suit having been filed on 28.12.66 was rightly found to be barred by limitation and it was also rightly found that the title of Satish Chandra and Protab Chandra and that of the plaintiff extinguished. The question of adverse possession having been rightly considered by the learned Judges of the High Court Division on consideration of the oral evidence on record the same calls for no interference. The question of limitation and adverse possession is a mixed question of law and fact and the same has been rightly decided in the appeal.
